Based on the retrieved healthcare Q&A matches, here is a synthesized clear and concise answer to the user's question:

Yes, size-reducing ascending aortoplasty with external reinforcement is currently considered an option in modern aortic surgery for patients with poststenotic dilatation of the aorta without impairment of the sinotubular junction of the aortic valve and root. This surgical technique aims to reduce the size of the ascending aorta while preserving the integrity of the sinotubular junction, allowing for safe and effective treatment.

In this procedure, an external reinforcement is placed around the aorta to help stabilize it and facilitate further reduction in diameter. The goal is to achieve optimal results with excellent long-term outcomes, making this technique a viable option for selected patients undergoing aortic surgery.
